Iñárritu (The Revenant (2015); Babel (2006); Birdman (2014)) and starring Tom Cruise (Top Gun (1986); Minority Report (2002); Mission: Impossible (1996); Rain Man (1988)), John Goodman (Argo (2012); Flight (2012); Kong: Skull Island (2017); Roseanne (tv series, 1988-2018)), Riz Ahmed (Jason Bourne (2016); Nightcrawler (2014); The Long Goodbye (short, 2020)) and Sandra Hüller (Requiem (2006); Anatomy of a Fall (2023); Project Hail Mary (2026)). A satirical comedy drama conveying a powerful message with a massive environmental impact: Rockwell (Tom Cruise) is a powerful oil magnate who lavishes far more attention on he ailing cat than he does on his family or staff, including Emma (Sandra Hüller). He is alerted to an impending disaster in Greenland where he has been extracting oil without regard for the consequences. He contacts US President Compson (John Goodman) who them brings his top aides, including military leaders, to his home so they can decide on which course of action to take, including perceptions of both political and economical perspectives, never environmental, despite keeping close to him his top environmental consultant, Ganesh (Riz Ahmed). Tom Cruise is excellent as Rockwell, particularly in a long monologue addressing a gallery of people only interested in baying for blood, while he is trying to spin it so that he is seen as the solution rather the problem; with fine performances too from John Goodman. This film will not be for everyone (it can be described as a polarising experience), as it is comparable to Wes Anderson's work (The Grand Budapest Hotel, Asteroic City, The French Dispatch, The Phoenician Scheme) and that of Yorgos Lanthimos (The Lobster, The Killing of a Sacred Deer). However, is does have a couple of profound twists, of which certainly the first really makes it as a film. Those that appreciate Digger will marvel at the cinematography and the thought-provoking messaging on both climate change and corporate greed, with the (drab) colour palette adding to the electricity of the performances. Digger is currently being screened at the Kinpeolis and CiNextDoor groups in Luxembourg. The murderer is called Benjamin William Day, he is a … Written by: Jack Williams Published on: October 11, 2026 He had transformed the room of an accommodation rented on Airbnb into a room to kill, trying to reproduce scenes from the television series Dexter. The murderer is called Benjamin William Day, he is a British student of forensic science and is just 20 years old. The young man pleaded guilty on October 6, during the second day of the trial, to killing Maria Saceanu, a 24-year-old Romanian woman. He will remain in custody awaiting sentencing, scheduled for December 4. The crime dates back to December 20, 2025, when Day was 19 years old. According to the reconstruction of the accusation reported by BBC the student had contacted Saceanu, who worked as an escort, through a website, using a phone purchased for that occasion. He then arranged to meet her in the rented room in Tividale, West Midlands. Before his arrival he had covered the walls and floor with plastic sheets and collected several objects: an apron, a protective visor and cleaning products. According to the prosecutor’s office, those preparations served to commit the murder and erase its traces. The reconstruction of the accusation and the reference to the TV series At the center of the trial was Day’s fascination with “Dexter”, the American series whose protagonist leads a double life: he works as a forensic expert for the police and is a serial murderer, capable of exploiting his skills to hide crimes. Prosecutor Rachel Brand argued that the young man had set up the room specifically to imitate the character. Saceanu was hit with 78 stab wounds. According to the medical examiner, his death was probably caused by injuries to his neck, with damage to the carotid arteries. The wounds on his hands were instead compatible with an attempt to defend himself. According to what was reported in court, Day had also started to dismember the body, but stopped after injuring his hand. The request for help and the attempted misdirection After leaving the accommodation, the young man walked away and, on the same night as the murder, called the British emergency number asking for medical assistance. In footage from officers’ body-worn cameras shown during the trial, he appeared sitting in a police car with one hand wrapped in duct tape. He told the police that he had gone to the Dudley area to drink and meet a girl in a bar, then claiming that he had been injured by an animal near a bush: perhaps a fox, perhaps a wild dog. The explanation had made the officers suspicious. The presence of the duct tape also raised questions: Day said he had taken it from his car, but could not remember where he had parked it. View this post on Instagram A post shared by West Midlands Police (@westmidlandspolice) Meanwhile, another guest of the facility had noticed a trail of blood and alerted the owner. Opening the door of the room, he saw the woman’s body, initially mistaken for a doll. The tip led the police to the crime scene. Day was arrested in the early hours of December 21st. He was wearing a khaki-colored shirt which, according to the prosecution, resembled that of the protagonist of the series. After just two days of court hearing, the young man admitted the murder. His lawyer asked for a report to be submitted to the judge before determining the sentence, citing the young age of the accused and the absence of a criminal record.
